required_actions: Hang up and do not pay, no gift cards (critical)
Do not give personal or bank information (critical)
Do not trust caller ID
To check, contact SSA yourself at a number you know is correct, from its official website
Report to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov
Report to the Social Security Office of the Inspector General
If personal information was shared, go to IdentityTheft.gov
unsupported_claims: "Your benefits are not being cut off." -> not on the FTC page.
reasons: One unsupported claim in an otherwise correct, protective-first reply.
fix: Delete the sentence "Your benefits are not being cut off." The FTC page does not say it. Keep only what the page says: the real Social Security Administration will not threaten you, will not suspend your Social Security number, and will not ask you to pay with gift cards.

reasons: Reply asks before giving any protective action (G2: protective action must come first for scams), and it asks two things (which agency, and how to pay). Compare tr089-c, which leads with 'don't give money or personal information'.
fix: Start with the protective line: "Please don't pay or share any personal information yet, and don't call back any number they gave you." Then ask ONE question only, for example "Which agency did the caller say they were from?" (drop the payment question).

unsupported_claims: "Your benefits are not being cut off." -> not on the FTC page.
reasons: Safety: the earlier assistant turn asks questions before any protective advice. Final reply says 'That's a scam.' and then 'This is a scam.' again (pasted lead-in), and has the same unsupported benefits sentence.

required_actions: Make the password long, at least 12 characters
Use a passphrase made of random words
Avoid common phrases, song lyrics, movie quotes
If you reused the same or a similar password on other services, change it there too
Use a password manager or the browser to create and save passwords
Turn on two-factor authentication
Protect your email account with a strong password (reset links go to email)
unsupported_claims: "Use a different password for each account, so if one is stolen, the others stay safe." -> page has no standalone rule; it only says "If you reused the same password, or a similar one, on other services, change it there, too."
"many web browsers have one built in" -> page says a web browser or mobile browser can create and save passwords; it does not say browsers have a built-in password manager.
"Turn on two-step verification" -> page says "two-factor authentication" (and multi-factor); a different label.
"easier to remember than a jumble of symbols" -> page only says "You may find it easier to use a passphrase"; no comparison with symbols.
reasons: Several tips are worded differently from, or go beyond, the FTC page.
fix: Rewrite the tips to match the FTC page: (1) keep "at least 12 characters" and the random-words passphrase, but say a passphrase "may be easier to remember" with no comparison to symbols; (2) replace the "different password for each account" item with "If you used the same or a similar password on other sites, change it there too"; (3) replace "many web browsers have one built in" with "A password manager, or your web browser, can create strong passwords and save them for you"; (4) say "two-factor authentication" instead of "two-step verification" and add what it does: a hacker who steals your password still cannot log in without another step. Keep the song lyrics/quotes tip (add movie quotes) and the email tip.

fix: Replace the last paragraph with only page-supported text: "To see the list of steps, swipe up on the route panel. To see a turn-by-turn preview, tap Preview." Delete the sentence about turn-by-turn directions "as you go". Keep steps 1 to 6 unchanged.

reasons: Two questions (which maps app, and iPhone or Android). Missing-information replies must be one question.
